arbaeen_ahadith.front: What level of religious knowledge is an obligation on us, according to the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A base level of religious literacy: knowing what is permissible and what is impermissible

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear” distinguish taqwā from waraʿ?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Taqwā, a defining quality of the believers, results in obeying Allah and avoiding His prohibitions. Waraʿ, the higher level, also leaves what is doubtful, keeping a safe distance from the ḥarām.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What teaching method of the Prophet ﷺ does the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear” show?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Teaching through examples, like the shepherd grazing near the sanctuary — one of his many methods

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What should someone do when unsure of a ruling, according to the lesson on the ḥadīth “the lawful is clear”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Ask those who know

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth “the religion is naṣīḥah” (Arbaʿīn 7)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Abū Ruqayyah Tamīm ibn Aws al-Dārī RA

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What was Tamīm al-Dārī RA before Islam, and when did he accept it?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A Christian — he accepted Islam in 9 AH

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Where did Tamīm al-Dārī RA go after ʿUthmān RA was martyred?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: To Shām — he settled in Palestine

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What was Tamīm al-Dārī RA known for?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: His night prayer, his piety and his worship

arbaeen_ahadith.front: When and where did Tamīm al-Dārī RA die?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: In 40 AH, in Palestine

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How many aḥādīth did Tamīm al-Dārī RA narrate?
What is said of the ḥadīth “the religion is naṣīḥah” as speech?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It is among the most eloquent of the Prophet's ﷺ words: in a few words it captures the whole Dīn

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is it said of Arbaʿīn 7, if all the other ḥadīth were lost?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That it alone would be enough

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does naṣīḥah mean, beyond sincere advice?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Sincerely wanting good for someone else — a desire for what is good for them

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How did Ibn Ḥajar define naṣīḥah?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Seeking good, or improvement, for the other person

arbaeen_ahadith.text: “The religion is naṣīḥah.” We said: “To whom?” He said: “To {{c1::Allah}}, to {{c2::His Book}}, to {{c3::His Messenger}}, and to {{c4::the leaders of the Muslims}} and {{c5::their common folk}}.”
arbaeen_ahadith.extra: <bdi>الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ</bdi> (Arbaʿīn 7, Muslim): the five relationships the Prophet ﷺ highlighted
arbaeen_ahadith.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 7 — the text in translation

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is naṣīḥah to Allah, first and foremost?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Believing in Him — His existence, oneness, might, power, glory and magnificence — and denying Him any partners

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Naṣīḥah to Allah also means {{c1::avoiding His prohibitions and following His commands}}, {{c2::remembering Him in every circumstance}}, {{c3::recognising His blessings and being grateful for them}}, and {{c4::being sincere in worship}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What must one believe about the Qurʾān, as naṣīḥah to Allah's Book?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: That it is Allah's uncreated word, given to the Prophet ﷺ — the greatest miracle ever given — and inimitable: nothing like it can ever be produced

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does naṣīḥah to the Qurʾān ask of us in practice?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: An active relationship with it — reciting it regularly, learning and teaching it, reflecting on its meanings and putting it into practice — and outward respect for it

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Naṣīḥah to the Messenger ﷺ: {{c1::believing he is Allah's last and final messenger}}; {{c2::loving and honouring him, and following what he told us}}; {{c3::behaving with the character the Sunnah teaches}}; {{c4::loving his household and his Companions}}; and {{c5::taking him as a role model in every aspect of life}}

Naṣīḥah to the leaders of the Muslims: {{c1::helping and obeying them in the truth}}; {{c2::ordering them with the truth and reminding them of it}}; {{c3::advising them of what they have neglected, and reminding them of the Muslims' rights}}; and {{c4::not rebelling against them with the sword, praying behind them, and supplicating for their correction}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who are “the leaders of the Muslims” in the ḥadīth “the religion is naṣīḥah”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Both the rulers and the scholars

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Naṣīḥah to the common folk: {{c1::guiding them to what will set their affairs right in both lives, and helping them in it}}; {{c2::protecting them from harm, helping them in need, and getting them what benefits them}}; {{c3::ordering good and forbidding evil, with kindness and sincerity}}; {{c4::showing them mercy — honouring their elders and being kind to the young}}; and {{c5::not cheating them, but supporting them}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What principle should govern each of the five relationships in the ḥadīth “the religion is naṣīḥah”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Give each its due rights and responsibilities — and stress one's responsibilities more than one's rights, to nurture the relationship and make it stronger

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is our relationship with Allah, according to the lesson on Arbaʿīn 7?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: One of submission, obedience and sincerity: He is the Lord, and we are His servants

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the foundation of our relationship with Allah, and how does it show itself?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Love, which expresses itself through hope and fear

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How is our relationship with Allah nurtured?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: By learning about Him, reflecting on His blessings, and expressing gratitude to Him

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Our relationship with the Qurʾān is that of student and teacher. What does it teach us?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The absolute truths and realities that form Islam's belief system, the relationship between man and his Creator, and the rules and regulations sent down in it

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Our relationship with the Prophet ﷺ is also that of student and teacher. What is he, for us?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The most perfect example of a human being: the ideal role model in every aspect of life, the physical manifestation of the Qurʾān, and the most noble in character and manners

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the foundation of our relationship with the Prophet ﷺ, and how is it nurtured?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Love, honour, respect and reverence — nurtured by learning about him, following his Sunnah, and sending abundant salutations on him

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is our default relationship with those in authority, and what limits it?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Obedience — but not absolute or unrestricted: there is no obedience to the creation in disobedience to the Creator (<bdi>لَا طَاعَةَ لِمَخْلُوقٍ فِي مَعْصِيَةِ الخَالِقِ</bdi>)

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why do Muslim citizens follow the law of the land by default, according to the lesson on Arbaʿīn 7?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Order, peace, security and safety in society are among Islam's priorities. So the law is followed by default, as long as it doesn't infringe personal rights and religious freedoms.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which field of study covers Islamic governance, including when disobedience, or in extreme cases revolt, is legitimate?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Al-siyāsah al-islāmiyyah (<bdi>السِّيَاسَة الإِسْلَامِيَّة</bdi>)

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does Islam view social behaviour and interaction?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: As one of the major components of its teachings. It puts great emphasis on family and community — Islam is not individualistic — and gives guidance for every communal and family role.

arbaeen_ahadith.text: How we must treat others: with {{c1::respect, kindness and care}}; {{c2::sympathy, compassion and generosity}}; and {{c3::love, mercy and forgiveness}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is Islam, beyond rituals and laws, or a creed and theology?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A complete way of life — including personal spiritual transformation (tazkiyah), excellent character (akhlāq), and how we deal with others

quduri.front: Why do the Ḥanafīs need more than an ordinary ḥadīth to allow wiping over footgear?
quduri.back: The verse of wuḍūʾ prescribes washing the feet. To move away from a ruling of the Qurʾān they require evidence of equal or greater weight: qaṭʿī al-thubūt and qaṭʿī al-dalālah.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: What evidence lets the Ḥanafīs allow wiping over the khuff instead of washing?
quduri.back: The aḥādīth on wiping have reached tawātur — al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said seventy Companions narrated it
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.meaning: a dispensation that makes life easier — like wiping over footgear, which replaces washing the feet
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.meaning: a leather sock that covers the whole foot, including the ankle
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.meaning: footgear of any material other than leather, such as cotton or wool
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: When may a Ḥanafī wipe over a jawrab, and why the condition?
quduri.back: When it functions like a khuff. Wiping over the khuff is agreed upon, but the aḥādīth that mention the jawrab are āḥād, not tawātur, so on their own they can't replace the washing the Qurʾān commands.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.text: The Ḥanafī conditions for wiping over a jawrab: it must {{c1::be of thick material, like wool}}; {{c2::stay on without being tied}}; {{c3::not be see-through}}; {{c4::cover the foot up to and including the ankles}}; {{c5::survive walking a fair distance, about 3.5 miles, without ripping}}; and {{c6::not let water seep through when wiped}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: What do the Ḥanafī conditions for a jawrab all come back to, and how were they derived?
quduri.back: The sock being thick, and so functioning like a khuff — they were derived through ijtihād
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.text: Conditions for wiping over footgear: it must {{c1::cover the whole foot, including the ankles}}; it must {{c2::have been put on while in a state of wuḍūʾ}}; and it must not {{c3::have a hole bigger than the area of one's three smallest toes}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: Which part of the footgear is wiped, and what is the minimum?
quduri.back: The top — at least the area of one's three smallest fingers
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: How is wiping over footgear done according to the Sunnah?
quduri.back: Begin at the toes with the fingers spread apart, and wipe once towards the shin
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: When does the time limit for wiping over footgear begin?
quduri.back: At the first nullification of wuḍūʾ after putting the footgear on
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: How long may a resident wipe over footgear, and how long a traveller?
quduri.back: A resident, one day and night (24 hours); a traveller, three full days (72 hours)
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: What must one do when the time limit for wiping runs out?
quduri.back: Wash the feet only — the whole wuḍūʾ needn't be repeated
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: Someone begins wiping as a resident, then travels before the 24 hours are up. How long may they wipe?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: Someone begins wiping as a traveller, then becomes a resident. What happens?
quduri.back: If they have already wiped for a day and night or more, they take the footgear off; if less, they complete the 24 hours
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.text: Wiping over footgear is nullified by {{c1::the end of the time limit}}, {{c2::taking the footgear off}}, and {{c3::anything that nullifies wuḍūʾ}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: Which coverings can't be wiped over by analogy with footgear?
quduri.back: The hijab or niqab, hats and gloves — there is no qiyās to them
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: How does wiping over a cast or bandage differ from wiping over footgear?
quduri.back: It is permitted even if the cast or bandage was put on without wuḍūʾ
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22

quduri.front: What becomes of wiping over a cast or bandage if it falls off before the wound has healed?
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: wiping over footgear — class notes 2026-10-22
